title: Cristaux et cohomologie de De Rham : généralités, correspondances Deligne et Berthelot (1965-1969) : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Context, from the neighbouring pages. A^{(ν)} is the truncated divided-power polynomial algebra over W (Witt vectors of a perfect field of characteristic p). It is generated by Λ_i = T^{[p^i]} for 0≤i≤ν, subject to Λ_i^p = c_i Λ_{i+1}, where c_i = (p^{i+1})!/(p^i!)^p has v_p(c_i)=1, and Λ_ν^p = 0.

The variable is then specialised to p. Put λ_i = γ_{p^i}(p) = p^{p^i}/(p^i)!, Θ_i = Λ_i − λ_i, and I = (Θ_0). Then W^{(ν)} = A^{(ν)}/I is the result of setting T = p in the truncated divided-power algebra. Equivalently, it is a truncated piece of the PD-envelope of the ideal pW in W when no compatibility with the canonical divided powers of p is imposed, i.e. W⟨T⟩/(T−p).

The previous page proves three things:
- p^i θ̇_i = 0 in W^{(ν)};
- p^{c(ν)} = 0 in W^{(ν)}, where c(ν) = ν + p·v_p(λ_ν) = ν + p(p^ν − (p^ν−1)/(p−1));
- a normal form for W^{(ν)}: Σ w_a θ̇^a with exponents 0≤a_i≤p−1, w_a ∈ E_i (representatives of W/p^i) if a_i is the first nonzero exponent, and w_0 ∈ E_{c(ν)}.

So W^{(ν)} is a finite W-module with a lot of torsion, and it is far from W/p^N.

This page relativises the result.
- Lemma. Let 1≤r≤ν and W^{(ν,r)} = W^{(ν)}/(θ̇_1,…,θ̇_r) = A^{(ν)}/I_{ν,r}, with I_{ν,r} = (Θ_0,…,Θ_r). Then Σ w_a Θ_0^{a_0}…Θ_ν^{a_ν} (exponents implicitly ≤ p−1) lies in I_{ν,r} iff two conditions hold:
  - (a) for a≠0 whose first nonzero coordinate a_i has i>r, w_a ∈ p^{i−r}W;
  - (b) w_0 ∈ p^{c(ν)−r}W.
  Coefficients of monomials whose first nonzero index is ≤ r are unconstrained, since those monomials are in the ideal.
- Corollary. Each element of W^{(ν,r)} has a unique normal form Σ w Θ_{r+1}^{a_{r+1}}…Θ_ν^{a_ν}, with w ∈ E_i when a_{r+i} is the first nonzero exponent, and w_0 ∈ E_{c(ν)−r}.

Mechanism. Expand (λ_i+Θ_i)^p = c_i(λ_{i+1}+Θ_{i+1}) and use λ_i^p = c_i λ_{i+1}. Once Θ_r is killed, c_r Θ_{r+1} ∈ I_{ν,r}, so pΘ_{r+1}=0. Inductively p^{j}Θ_{r+j}=0. Finally p^{ν−r}Θ_ν=0 together with Λ_ν^p=0 gives p^{ν−r}λ_ν^p = 0, whose valuation is c(ν)−r.

Check at r=ν: W^{(ν,ν)} = W/p^{c(ν)−ν} = W/p^{v(λ_ν^p)}. This is exactly what one expects: all Θ_i vanish, so the only surviving relation is λ_ν^p = Λ_ν^p = 0.

Purpose. This is an explicit structure computation of the divided-power algebra in which the variable is specialised to p, i.e. a non-compatible PD-envelope of (p) in W. It belongs to the 'généralités' on crystals: it shows concretely the torsion that appears when PD structures are not required to be compatible with the canonical divided powers on pW. The next page restarts the presentation of A^{(ν)} and its monomial reduction lemma.
errors: The lemma does not state the exponent range 0≤a_i≤p−1. It is implicit from the normal-form context, and without it the criterion would be false, since Θ_i^p is not a monomial of the stated type.
In the Corollary the exponent bounds 0≤a_{r+i}≤p−1 are omitted, and the generators are written as undotted Θ although they are images in W^{(ν,r)}. These are minor notational slips.

Condition (a) silently allows arbitrary coefficients when the first nonzero index is ≤ r. This is correct, but implicit. The phrase 'Pour que … il faut et il suffit' is proved only by analogy with the previous page (the 'I' is an ideal' check is left to the reader).
No mathematical error found. The orders p^{i−r} and the exponent c(ν)−r check out via v_p(c_i)=1 and v_p(λ_ν^p)=c(ν)−ν.

ideas.what: Explicit W-module structure (normal form) of the truncated divided-power algebra W⟨T⟩_{<p^{ν+1}} with T specialised to p, and of its quotients by θ̇_1..θ̇_r
ideas.modern_name: PD-envelope / divided power algebra computations; torsion in non-compatible PD-envelopes of (p)
ideas.usually_credited_to: General PD-envelope theory: Berthelot (Cohomologie cristalline, 1974); compatibility condition for divided powers: Berthelot / Grothendieck
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck's 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (IHES notes, Dix exposés) discusses the need for divided powers but, to my knowledge, not this explicit computation; unsure

ideas.what: Use of the valuation of γ_{p^i}(p)=p^{p^i}/p^i! and of c_i=(p^{i+1})!/(p^i!)^p having v_p=1 to derive the torsion orders p^i, p^{i−r} and p^{c(ν)−r}
ideas.modern_name: Legendre formula / p-adic valuation of divided powers

missed.claim: An explicit, fully worked normal form for W⟨T⟩/(T−p) (truncated at degree p^{ν+1}) and its quotients by the first r divided-power defects, with exact torsion exponents c(ν)−r. This quantifies the failure of a non-compatible PD-envelope of (p) to equal W. The phenomenon itself is well known qualitatively, but such explicit tables are rarely written out.
missed.quote: Pour que ∑ w_a Θ_0^{a_0}⋯Θ_ν^{a_ν} soit dans I_{ν,r}, il faut et il suffit que … w_a ∈ p^{i−r}W … w_0 ∈ p^{c(ν)−r}W
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is of mild interest for explicit computations of PD-envelopes, prismatic and crystalline comparisons, and examples of torsion in non-flat PD-envelopes. It is mostly a pedagogical or historical detail.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but routine explicit computation of torsion in a specialised divided-power algebra, serving the foundations of crystalline cohomology. The result is correct and elementary, and the qualitative phenomenon is standard. Only the explicit normal form is an unpublished detail.
transcription_corrections: The opening '} w_0 ∈ E_{c(ν)}' is the tail of the Corollary on the previous page (normal form in W^{(ν)}), not part of the Lemma.
In the Lemma, 'Θ̇_1,…,Θ̇_r' should be read as the images θ̇_i in W^{(ν)}, while Θ_0,…,Θ_r live in A^{(ν)} (where Θ_i = Λ_i − λ_i).
'W^{(ν,r)}§.' is just 'W^{(ν,r)}.' followed by a stray mark.
The struck-out part of item a) reads '∀ α, 1≤α≤ν−r, premier' and is replaced by the inserted 'a=(a_0,…,a_ν)≠0, si a_i est le premier composant non nul et si i>r'.
In the Corollary, the boldface 'E_i' overwrites a scribbled earlier subscript, and 'qui est ≠ 0' completes the condition.
